description: Phase-DEFER — lift Anthropic Claude Code's deferred-tools pattern into Aura's tool registry, starting with execute_code + execute_shell. Pre-cursor to Phase-MCP-UI: when MCP server count grows, having the deferred infrastructure in place means tools enter as name-only manifest entries, with full JSON schema loaded lazily via tool_search. Today: kills the always-on schema cost of execute_code (~400 tokens) and execute_shell (~400 tokens) — those are heavyweight tools the LLM doesn't need every turn. Source pattern: Anthropic Claude Code's ToolSearch behavior (verbatim, see chat 2026-05-23 — deferred tools listed by name in system reminder, schema fetched via `ToolSearch(query="select:<name>")`). NOT to be confused with Phase-TOOL's killed tool RAG router (embedding-based intercept of agent loop) — this is tool_search-as-TOOL (LLM-invokable, heuristic-only). 3 stories, ~250 LOC. Per-module deep refactor on touch mandatory per CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: Tool registry — add Deferred flag + split manifest renderer
userStories.description: Add `Deferred bool` to the Tool registration interface (likely internal/agent/tools/registry.go or wherever ToolSpec lives). Default false (backward-compatible — every existing tool stays always-on until explicitly marked). Update the manifest renderer that builds the system-prompt tool surface so it emits TWO sections: (a) always-on tools → full JSON schema in the LLM-facing manifest, (b) deferred tools → just `{name, brief_description}` (one line, ≤200 chars). userStories.title: tool_search tool — name-only / keyword / select query forms
userStories.description: Add `tool_search` as a real always-on tool in internal/agent/tools/registry/tool_search.go. The LLM calls it when it wants to invoke a deferred tool: `tool_search(query: "select:execute_code")` → returns the full JSON schema. Three query forms (mirror Claude Code's ToolSearch verbatim where possible): (a) `select:Name1,Name2` — exact name fetch, deterministic; (b) `keyword1 keyword2` — heuristic search by name + description with TF-IDF-style scoring; (c) `+required keyword` — require term + rank by remaining. Result is a JSON envelope: `{tools: [{name, description, parameters: {...full JSON Schema...}}]}` — the LLM gets the schema inline as a tool result. From the NEXT turn, the LLM can invoke the deferred tool by name as normal (the registry will accept the call regardless of schema-load state — schema is for the LLM's prompt, runtime dispatch doesn't need it pre-loaded). Implementation: pure CPU heuristic (no embedding, no LLM-as-router — Phase-TOOL killed those anti-patterns). max_results parameter (default 5, max 20). Source pattern: openhuman harness/tool_filter.rs + Claude Code's verbatim ToolSearch interface.

userStories.notes: DEPENDS ON US-DEFER-01 + US-DEFER-02. This is the validating story — proves the infrastructure works end-to-end with two real production tools. After this lands, future tools (especially MCP-driven ones) can be deferred trivially by setting the flag at registration. RISK: LLM may fail to call tool_search and just try to invoke execute_shell directly. That's actually OK because runtime dispatch doesn't need the schema — but the LLM may get arg shape wrong without seeing the schema. Mitigation: the AGENT.md hint is the prompt-side instruction. If empirically the LLM struggles, a future story can add an inline 'this tool requires tool_search first' note in the deferred manifest entry.
